messages:
Sonal: Heads up — bringing up the eu-west-2 GPU cluster (8xA100-80GB per node) this afternoon. I want a short, runnable perf validation runbook we can follow for bootstrap -> validation -> handoff. Can we agree on commands, thresholds, and where to stash results?

Marco: +1. I'll lay out a checklist we can run in 20–30m per node. Minimal automation but all commands should be copy-paste.

Priya: Important items to include: kernel & driver sanity, CUDA + cuDNN, NCCL + RDMA checks, filesystem throughput, NVMe health, and an LLM microbenchmark for throughput/latency. Also record MTU checks and switch ECN/DSCP settings if applicable.

Dan: I'll add expected baseline numbers for our standard inference profile (batch=1, seq=512 for latency; batch=8 for throughput). Typical targets for A100-80GB in our infra: p50 < 110ms, p95 < 200ms for batch=1; tokens/sec ~ 1800–2200 for batch=8 (model: open-llama-13B-ish). These are rough — we'll capture exact numbers during validation.

Sonal: Good. Can someone paste the actual commands we should run? Keep them simple.

Marco: Here you go — run as root or with sudo. Put outputs in /tmp/perf-validate then scp to s3://redwood-perf/eu-west-2/<node>/timestamp/

Marco: ```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/perf-validate
uname -a > /tmp/perf-validate/uname.txt
modinfo nvidia | head -n 40 > /tmp/perf-validate/modinfo.txt
nvidia-smi -q -d SUPPORTED_CLOCKS,DRIVER_VERSION -f /tmp/perf-validate/nvidia-smi.txt
nvidia-smi topo -m > /tmp/perf-validate/topo.txt
lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,ROTA,MOUNTPOINT > /tmp/perf-validate/lsblk.txt
nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1 > /tmp/perf-validate/nvme0.txt || true
ethtool -i eth0 > /tmp/perf-validate/eth0-driver.txt
ip link show eth0 > /tmp/perf-validate/eth0-link.txt
ip route get 8.8.8.8 > /tmp/perf-validate/route.txt
sysctl net.core.rmem_max net.core.wmem_max > /tmp/perf-validate/sysctl.txt
# NCCL / RDMA
which ibv_devinfo >/dev/null 2>&1 && ibv_devinfo > /tmp/perf-validate/ibv_devinfo.txt || echo "no rdma" > /tmp/perf-validate/ibv_devinfo.txt
# basic network throughput
iperf3 -c <test-server> -t 20 -P 4 > /tmp/perf-validate/iperf3.txt || true
# microbench: llm-bench (our internal script)
llm-bench --model open-13b --batch 1 --seq 512 --iters 20 --device cuda > /tmp/perf-validate/latency_b1_s512.txt
llm-bench --model open-13b --batch 8 --seq 512 --iters 100 --device cuda > /tmp/perf-validate/throughput_b8_s512.txt
# basic GPU mem and temp
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.total,memory.used,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu --format=csv > /tmp/perf-validate/gpu-summary.csv
# tar results
cd /tmp && tar czf /tmp/perf-validate.tar.gz perf-validate
# upload
aws s3 cp /tmp/perf-validate.tar.gz s3://redwood-perf/eu-west-2/$(hostname)/$(date +%s)/
``` 

Priya: Nice. A couple of additions: run dmesg | grep -i nvrm or nvidia errors, and verify kernel params: dmesg | tail -n 200 > dmesg.txt. Also check that driver module is pinned: lsmod | grep nvidia. Add those to the script.

Dan: Thresholds I'll use when reviewing:
- Driver: NVIDIA driver >= 535.XX, CUDA >= 12.1.
- nvidia-smi reports no ECC errors and GPU temp < 85C under load.
- NVMe: avg latency < 1ms for 128k sequential reads (fio sample).
- Network: iperf3 >= 20Gbps on 100Gbps links; MTU 9000 enabled for RDMA nodes.
- LLM microbench: p50 latency within ±20% of reference (reference stored in s3://redwood-perf/reference/eu-west-2/). Throughput within ±25%.

Marco: Add quick fio commands to validate NVMe:```bash
fio --name=seqread --filename=/dev/nvme0n1 --rw=read --bs=128k --size=4G --numjobs=1 --time_based --runtime=30 --group_reporting > /tmp/perf-validate/fio-read.txt
```

Sonal: What about kernel modules & driver mismatches? We had a bad rollout last month where the distro kernel didn't match the dkms-built driver. How do we catch that?

Marco: Check:```bash
uname -r
modinfo nvidia | grep vermagic || true
# if vermagic doesn't match uname -r then driver was built against a different kernel
``` If mismatched, mark node as FAIL and escalate to eng-ops for rebuild.

Priya: Network specifics: for RDMA-enabled clusters run this after ibv_devinfo:```bash
rdma_pingpong -d mlx5_0 -S 10.0.0.1 > /tmp/perf-validate/rdma_ping.txt || echo "rdma test fail" > /tmp/perf-validate/rdma_ping.txt
``` If RDMA fails, classify as P1 — it will impact multi-node model sharding.

Dan: For latency baselining, include a small end-to-end inference check against our local model server:```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -d '{"model":"open-13b","input":"Hello world"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -w "\nTIME_TOTAL:%{time_total}\n" > /tmp/perf-validate/httptest.txt
``` Capture time_total and compare with reference.

Sonal: Where do we put pass/fail criteria and sign-off? I want a simple matrix in the ticket so SRE can sign off.

Marco: Let's use a small JSON status file we upload alongside artifacts: /tmp/perf-validate/status.json with keys: driver_ok, nvme_ok, network_ok, llm_ok, rdma_ok, human_signoff. We'll upload and then create the ticket linking the S3 path. Example status.json:```json
{"driver_ok":"PASS","nvme_ok":"PASS","network_ok":"WARN:MTU mismatch","llm_ok":"PASS","rdma_ok":"FAIL","human_signoff":"pending"}
```

Priya: Handoff steps after all PASS:
1) Create GH issue in infra/region-rollouts with artifacts link.
2) Ping #eng-oncall and #eng-sre with summary and sign-off tag.
3) Mark cluster as available in inventory and update autoscaler config.
4) Schedule 24h follow-up to check stability metrics.

Sonal: Sounds good. Can we automate the status.json creation from script?

Marco: Yes — I'll add a tiny python snippet at the end that parses outputs and generates the status.json with the thresholds Dan listed. Will push to the repo under infra/scripts/perf-validate.sh and perf-validate-parse.py.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: infra/scripts/perf-validate.sh v1.2 deployed to eu-west-2 staging at 1718956890

oncall-bot: Reminder: please include the S3 artifact link in the handoff ticket. Auto-ack if status.json has all PASS.

Dan: After we run the script on all nodes, I'll review S3 artifacts. If everything is green, I'll mark the region rollout as signed-off and add baseline numbers to s3://redwood-perf/reference/eu-west-2/. If there are WARN/FAIL items we either remediate (driver rebuild, MTU fix) or escalate depending on severity.

Sonal: OK — we will run this now on the first 3 nodes and post results. I'll ping when done. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Marco: TL;DR checklist (for quick copy):
- kernel & modinfo check
- nvidia-smi & topo
- dmesg scan for driver errors
- fio NVMe check
- iperf3 & MTU check
- ibv_devinfo & RDMA ping (if applicable)
- llm-bench latency & throughput runs
- curl end-to-end timing
- gen status.json and upload artifacts
- create GH issue + ping oncall for signoff

Sonal: posted results: s3://redwood-perf/eu-west-2/node-03/1718957105/perf-validate.tar.gz — will open ticket now.

Priya: I'll review logs for RDMA and NVMe, ping if anything weird.

Dan: I'll pull the artifacts now. If green I'll attach baseline and close the loop.
